body: Forgot to mention I tried --rendering-driver opengl3 and it works perfectly fine with no crash, so this is specifically related to Forward+

Hi! Thanks for reporting — this looks like a Vulkan device/lost/fence wait crash, but it’s hard to narrow down without a reproducible case.

Could you share a few more details?

**System / drivers**
- NVIDIA driver version (exact number):
- Laptop model (or GPU power limits / mux mode if applicable):
- Does the issue persist after a clean driver reinstall?

**Repro / settings**
- Does it happen in **Forward+ only**, or also in **Mobile** (Vulkan Mobile renderer)?
- Does it change if you toggle: VSync (on/off), fullscreen vs windowed, MSAA, SSAO, screen-space reflections, GI, etc.?
- If you can, please try with a **fresh empty project** (Forward+) and see if it ever crashes.

**Logs**
- When it crashes, can you attach `godot.log` (or editor output) and any crash dump (if generated)?
- If possible, please share the exact command line you used (you mentioned `--accurate-breadcrumbs`).

Also, once the **MRP** is ready, that will be the biggest help for devs to reproduce/fix.

Hi friend,

- NVIDIA Drivers tested: 591.86 - 591.44 - 581.80
- Laptop model: MSI Vector 16 HX AI, TDP PL1: 140W PL2: 220W TDP:175W, MUX: yes, Optimus MSHybrid
- Yes I had this issue since June 2025, it never disappeared

**Repro / settings**
- Tested only Forward+ & OpenGL (openGL is fine) I will be testing mobile renderer later but as I'm writing this I might have found the culprit!! (read below)
- Crashes on all resolution (fullscreen, windowed)
- I tested every settings, AA, Post processing and found some infos: The game can last much longer before crashing if I disable BOTH Anti-aliasing & Post Processing, but it still ends up crashing eventually after 5 minutes or so.
- I tried Shadows disabled/enabled, VSync, still leads to crashes
- Disabling SDFGI seem to completely stops crashing & has even made my FPS much more stable (no more drops on each events like it used to) I think this is even the culprit, I'll keep using it with sdfgi disabled and tell you if it crashes but for the moment it seem fixed so far

- Command I use start "Client1" "C:\Users\Morland\Documents\GitHub\GClash-godot\Godot_v4.6-stable_win64.exe" --main-scene "res://startup_scene.tscn" --accurate-breadcrumbs (added accurate-breadcrumbs when I started trying to debug the crashes but it gives no more infos)

Find attached as well godot.log

[godot.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25268712/godot.log)

Fast forward from all my testing, disabling sdfgi fixed it!! Game went from crashing randomly in less than 10 minutes to being stable after 1 hour of gameplay with much less FPS drops as well, so this might be it, now remains the question if it's a RTX 50 series compatibility issue with sdfgi or something else!

Ok so it's been over 24h I've thoroughly tested and I confirm: disabling SDFGI completely fixed it; When having sdfgi enabled all I get is unstable frames with random freeze that leads to a crash within 5 minutes max.

I have a very similar callstack, but no MRP, because at the moment it only happens on my full game with a quite deep stack of viewports and shaders. The callstack originates within an atmosphere shader from https://github.com/Zylann/godot_atmosphere_shader (not saying it is the culprit, just the crash trigger) and ~only when SDFGI is enabled~. After some time running the project, this now happens even with SDFGI disabled.
